# Software Design Document (SDD)

<!-- Generated by `omni docs build` (REQ-060) for OmniEngineering Workspace. Do not edit; regenerate. -->

What each part of OmniEngineering Workspace is for: 4 module(s) in 1 package(s). Each package gets one line in the table below, then one line per module: its purpose (from the module docstring), the public types it defines, how many project modules import it, and the design reason when the docstring gives one.

Where the rest lives: per-module import lists in the [Module Reference](modules.md), class relationships in the [Class Diagram](class-diagram.md), which files and tests belong to each requirement in the [Requirements Traceability Matrix](requirements-traceability.md). `omni docs build --detail full` writes every public signature, class and method here instead.

## Package repository root

- [make_ai.py](../../make_ai.py): _No module docstring._ Defines `DoctorReport`. 203 public functions. Imported by 1 module.
- [omni_docs.py](../../omni_docs.py): REQ-060: `omni docs build` -- standard engineering documents and Mermaid diagrams, generated without a model. Defines `PyFunc`, `PyClass`, `PyInfo`, `Module` (+3 more). 47 public functions. Imported by 1 module. Why: Every document is derived from data the workspace already keeps: the code graph (`.ai/project-graph.json`), the requirement registry, the failure ledger, the test-suite registry, git history (as recorded in the graph's history layer)...
- [omni_graph.py](../../omni_graph.py): Deterministic, local source-code graph built from tree-sitter ASTs. Defines `GraphDependencyError`, `GraphNode`, `GraphEdge`, `Graph` (+1 more). 63 public functions. Imported by 2 modules.
- [omni_mcp.py](../../omni_mcp.py): A minimal MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over stdio, exposing the graph and registries as tools. Defines `MCPTool`, `ToolError`. 3 public functions. Why: Deliberately hand-rolled against the wire protocol (JSON-RPC 2.0, newline-delimited, over stdin/stdout) rather than depending on an MCP SDK: this workspace works across assistants, machines and Python versions with only the standard...
